data.about: A uniformly loaded cable hangs as a parabola — and this drawing builds that parabola three different ways through the same two supports A, B and apex C. First the MIDPOINT RULE: on any vertical the curve lies exactly midway between a secant and a tangent, so halving repeatedly gives the apex (h below the closing string, where the support tangents meet 2h below), then the quarter points, then the eighths. Second the FUNICULAR: parallels to the support tangents through the ends of the load line fix the pole o, and the rays hang a polygon through every one of those points. Third the TANGENT METHOD: divide the two support tangents into eight equal parts and join the k-th mark of one to the k-th of the other — every line touches the curve, which appears as the envelope of its own tangents.

steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: supports A and B on the walls, apex C on the centreline — span l, half-span l/2 (drag A, B, C)
steps.title: Three points define the parabola

steps.caption: left: the distributed load q with its total resultant R at midspan — right: the same total load R laid off as the load line
steps.title: The uniform load q — its resultant R

steps.caption: left: the closing string A–B crosses the centreline; the apex C hangs the rise h below it
steps.title: Closing string and rise h

steps.caption: left: mirroring that crossing about C gives the point 2h below the closing string — the tangents at the supports will meet there
steps.title: Mirror: 2h below the closing string

steps.caption: left: tangents A and B through the mirror point — right: parallels to them through the ends of the load line intersect at the pole o
steps.title: Tangents at the supports → the pole o

steps.caption: right: the outer rays are the two reactions — left: the same pulls at the supports, along the tangents
steps.title: Reactions A and B

steps.caption: left: secants A–C and C–B, and the tangent at C parallel to the closing string — right: the mid ray o–F₃ is parallel to both and halves the load line
steps.title: Secants to the apex — tangent at C

steps.caption: left: THE rule that draws a parabola — on any vertical, the curve lies exactly MIDWAY between a secant and a tangent. Take the quarter verticals: the secant A–C and the tangent at A cut them; halve the black segment between the two marked points (y = y) and you have a parabola point — right: the load line splits into the node loads R
steps.title: The midpoint rule

steps.caption: right: rays from o to the quarter cuts — left: the strings A–C and C–B refine into four strings, each parallel to its ray
steps.title: A first funicular: quarters

steps.caption: left: halve once more: secant and tangent on each eighth vertical, midway between them the curve — four more parabola points, nine in all — right: the load line splits into eight node loads R
steps.title: The rule again — eighth points

steps.caption: right: rays from o to every cut — left: the funicular polygon 1…8 through all nine points, each member parallel to its ray
steps.title: The funicular polygon

steps.caption: left: forget the verticals — mark the two support tangents A–T and T–B in eight EQUAL parts each, numbered towards the meeting point and away from it
steps.title: A third way: the tangent method

steps.caption: left: join the k-th mark of one tangent to the k-th of the other: EVERY one of those lines touches the parabola — the curve appears as the envelope of its own tangents, without computing a single point
steps.title: Join 1 to 1, 2 to 2, …

steps.caption: left: consecutive tangent intersections trace the enclosing polygon of the same parabola (the funicular polygon touches it from inside)
steps.title: The enclosing polygon

steps.caption: the construction retires — the funicular of the uniform load is the parabola through A, C and B, all members pink = tension
steps.title: Tension
